about.title: Fremont Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Fourteen people died on Fremont roads in 2025, according to the most recent final crash records for the city. Behind each of those numbers is a household in Alameda County trying to make sense of a Friday evening commute on I-880 or a turn off Fremont Boulevard that never ended the way it should have. A wrongful death claim will not undo any of that. What it can do is hold the responsible party financially accountable and help the people left behind stay steady. Under California law, the right to bring the claim belongs first to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children; certain dependents and heirs may qualify after them. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it shrinks considerably when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Fremont families with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless something is recovered.

whyChoose.title: Why Fremont Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can sort out which family members belong on the claim before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, but the window is far shorter if a government entity is involved. Starting now protects that timeline.

items.title: Losses that get counted
items.desc: Recoverable damages include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. A contingency-fee attorney pursues all of it with no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: If the other driver is facing criminal charges in Alameda County, do we still need a civil case?
items.answer: Yes, the two are separate. A criminal prosecution is brought by the district attorney and focuses on punishment, not on compensating your family. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that can move forward whether or not charges are filed or result in a conviction.

items.question: Our family member died in a crash on I-680 in Fremont. Does the two-year deadline still apply?
items.answer: Usually, but be cautious. If a road condition or a public vehicle contributed to the death, a claim against a government entity like the state or the city may be required, and that process carries a much shorter deadline than two years. An attorney can review the collision facts quickly to see whether the shorter clock is running.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge our family anything?
items.answer: No. Our connection service is free, and we are not a law firm. The independent attorney you are matched with works on contingency, meaning there is no attorney fee unless money is recovered for your family.
